title: Houston Weather: Calm and cloudy conditions continue this week, slim rain chance - ABC13 Houston

Houston Weather: Calm and cloudy conditions continue this week, slim rain chance - ABC13 Houston 
 24/7 Live Houston Southwest Southeast Northwest Northeast Need to Know Weather 
 Calm and cloudy conditions continue this week, slim rain chance 
 We'll keep these cloudy and calm conditions throughout much of the week, and by Wednesday it'll start to feel a bit muggier out too. By Travis Herzog , David Tillman , Elita Loresca , Kevin Roth , Elyse Smith Sunday, October 25, 2026 11:32PM Share Follow ABC13 on Google HOUSTON, Texas (KTRK) -- We'll keep these cloudy and calm conditions throughout much of the week, and by Wednesday it'll start to feel a bit muggier out too. Rain chances are slim until we head into November.
 The high levels clouds outside this evening should lead to a gorgeous sunset and will stick around overnight. Temperatures will fall from the upper 70s into the upper 50sby Monday morning. And Monday will look and feel pretty similar to Sunday with these high-level clouds and comfortable temps with highs in the low 80s.
 How much longer does the dry air and lower humidity stick around?
 This comfortable fall air should be with us through Tuesday. Muggy air will return to our coastal communities sooner than that, but by Wednesday all of us will be in that muggy air. This will increase our morning lows into the mid-to-upper 60s. This moisture increase also sets the stage for our rise in storm chances around Halloween and into early November.
 How stormy does it look for Halloween?
 It's too soon to say exactly how the weather will unfold on Halloween, but we are sniffing out a stormier weather pattern developing toward the end of next week. At a minimum, we should prepare for a warm, humid day with a chance of thunderstorms. Right now we have the coverage at 30%, so it looks likely we avoid a holiday washout. Parents should be aware though of the risk for lightning with these isolated storms and any outdoor activities on Saturday.
 And what about for Election Day?
 The stormy weather pattern lingers and there's even the chance for more rainy weather around Election Day. A big dip in the jet stream could send a strong storm system to the state of Texas around Election Day or just thereafter. This is the kind of weather pattern that wouldn't only bring rain but also the chance for strong storms too. It's a bit too early to nail down the exact timing and impacts, but as of now expect to use the umbrella a little more in the early days of November, which we'll need the rain by that point too!
 What are you tracking in the tropics?
 We are keeping a watchful eye Hurricane Vance in the eastern Pacific that could eventually send some moisture toward Texas late next week. For a more in-depth discussion on what's happening in the tropics, visit our Daily Tropical Update page .
